>_ Project Overview
THE MISSION
Build and deploy a complete, production-ready web platform that integrates a live AI API feature you author
yourself. The site must be publicly accessible, properly secured, and include at least one page or feature powered
by a real AI API call written server-side -- no plugins, no copy-paste embeds.
THE RULES
> Individual project (no partners this time)
> Must be live-hosted with a real URL (VPS or shared hosting)
> Submitted online by May 3rd 2026, 11:59 PM
> Worth 150 points
>_ Tier 1: Infrastructure (50 pts)
> Live Hosting VPS or shared hosting with a real public URL
> Custom Domain DNS configured and pointing to your server
> SSL/TLS Let's Encrypt certificate installed (green padlock)
> HTTPS Redirect 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS
> Firewall UFW or equivalent, only ports 22/80/443 open
> Web Server Nginx or Apache configured with proper server blocks
>_ Tier 2: AI Integration (70 pts)
> Server-Side API Call PHP, Python, or Node script handles the API request (key never in browser)
> Contextual Feature AI feature matches the site's purpose (not just a generic chatbot)
> Custom System Prompt You wrote and tuned the prompt -- not default API behavior
> Error Handling API failure shows a graceful message, not a PHP error or blank page
> Live and Functional Feature works on your submitted URL at grading time
> Nginx Proxy Config API endpoint routed through your web server, not exposed directly
>_ What Your AI Feature Could Look Like
Pick a site concept. Build a feature that makes sense for it.
> Restaurant site Visitor enters dietary restrictions, AI suggests menu items
> Portfolio site AI chatbot answers questions about your skills, grounded in your bio
> Local business site AI assistant answers FAQs about hours, services, and location
> Tech blog Visitor pastes a topic, AI generates a reading summary or outline
Approved AI Providers
> OpenAI (GPT-4o mini -- free tier available) | Anthropic Claude | Google Gemini | Cohere
> Hard rule: API key must live in a server-side file. Never in HTML, JS, or the browser.
>_ Tier 3: Professional Polish (30 pts)
Documentation (15 pts)
> Tech stack manifest: OS, web server, language runtime, AI provider used
> Written explanation of your AI feature: what it does, why you built it that way
> Screenshot of the AI feature working live in the browser
LinkedIn Portfolio Artifact (15 pts)
> Post or "Project" entry on LinkedIn with screenshot
> Tag hard skills: #Linux #Nginx #SSL #WebOps #AI #APIIntegration #PromptEngineering
> Link to your live URL in the post
>_ Grading Rubric

Tier 1 Infrastructure (Hosting, DNS, SSL,
Firewall, Web Server) 50
Tier 2 AI Integration (Server-Side API,
Prompt, Error Handling, Proxy) 70

>_ CMS Options for Your Platform
Traditional CMS -- Best for most projects
> WordPress Most plugins, most tutorials, most forgiving. PHP + MySQL. Strong choice.
> Ghost Node.js, clean and fast, great for blogs and content-first sites. Modern feel.
> Drupal Enterprise-grade, steeper learning curve, impressive on a resume if you pull it off.
Headless CMS -- Advanced option, extra credit worthy
> WordPress as Headless WP REST API delivers content, custom frontend consumes it
> Strapi or Contentful API-first CMS, pairs cleanly with a custom frontend and AI endpoint
Bottom line: Pick what you can deploy, secure, and explain. Complexity only earns points if it works.
>_ AI API Options -- Pick Your Provider
> OpenAI GPT-4o mini is fast, cheap, and well-documented. Best free-tier option to start. REST API, PHP-friendly.
> Anthropic Claude Strong at instruction-following and custom persona. Good for chatbot and FAQ features.
> Google Gemini Free tier via Google AI Studio. Good if you are already in the Google ecosystem.
> Cohere Solid free tier, great for text classification and summarization use cases.
How the Call Works -- Every Provider Follows This Pattern
> 1. System prompt You define the AI persona and rules in your server script
> 2. User message Visitor input passed from your form to your PHP/Python script
> 3. POST to API Your server sends the request using curl or an HTTP library
> 4. Response returned JSON parsed, AI reply rendered on the page for the visitor
>_ A Note on Grading
Grading is not purely mechanical. Here is what that means.
> The rubric is the floor, not the ceiling. Content quality, presentation, and effort inform the final score.
> Attendance, participation, and classroom engagement are part of how your work is understood and evaluated.
> A technically complete submission from someone who never showed up reads very differently than the same work
from someone who was present and engaged.
Regrades
> I do not regrade. The score you receive is considered final.
> If you want to understand your score in more detail, send me an email. I will walk you through exactly what I saw and
why.
> That conversation is worth having. Not to change the number, but to understand what excellence looks like.
>_ Connections -- People Buy from People
Your resume gets you in the room. Your network gets you the call before the job is even posted.
What you should already be doing
> Attend local tech events. Philly Tech Week, AWS meetups, WordPress Meetup, OWASP chapter -- these are free and full
of hiring managers.
> Talk to people outside your classroom. Professors, guest speakers, alumni, career center contacts. One warm intro
beats 100 cold applications.
> Post your work publicly. This project is your proof of work. LinkedIn, GitHub, your portfolio URL -- make it findable.
> Send the follow-up. After every event, connect on LinkedIn within 24 hours with a personal note referencing what you
talked about.
> Be useful, not just visible. Share what you build. Comment thoughtfully on others’ posts. Add value before asking for
anything.
The goal: By the time you graduate, someone outside this classroom should know your name and what you can do.
>_ CPT & OPT Students -- This Is for You
Your timeline is tighter and your path to employment requires more deliberate action. Start now.
Your project is your visa-independent proof of skill
> A live URL with a working AI feature is something you can show in any interview, regardless of your status. Build it
well.
> Document your GitHub. Employers sponsoring H-1B need to justify the hire -- your portfolio makes that case for you.
Networking is not optional -- it is the strategy
> Target employers who have sponsored visas before. Use myvisajobs.com to find companies with a history of H-1B
sponsorship.
> Connect with people who look like you on LinkedIn. Find alumni from your country at companies you want to work for.
They will often respond.
> Know your CPT/OPT deadlines cold. Your DSO and international student office are your allies. Meet with them before
you need them.
Final thought: Your visa status is a fact, not a limitation. You’re in good shape: the hardest part for the “portfolio + AI” option is having real content (skills, education, projects). Your existing site gives you that—you mainly need deployment that meets Tier 1, a **server-side** chat endpoint that Tier 2 requires, and polish + docs for Tier 3.

---

## 1. What to ship (portfolio + contextual chatbot)

**Visitor experience:** Someone lands on your portfolio, opens “Ask about me” (or similar), types a question, and gets answers **grounded in your résumé**—not a generic ChatGPT persona.

That matches the rubric: **contextual**, **your system prompt**, **API key never in the browser**.

**Minimum viable AI page:**

- Short intro: “I’m [name]. Ask about my stack, education, projects, or how to reach me.”
- Text area + Submit (no key in frontend—only POST to **your** path, e.g. `/api/chat` or `/ask.php`).
- Loading state + **graceful error** if the provider is down/rate-limited (“Something went wrong—try again or email …”).

---

## 2. Architecture that graders expect

Roughly:

```
Browser → HTTPS → Nginx (your domain)
           ├→ static/HTML (or WP) … your portfolio
           └→ `/api/chat` proxied to local app (PHP/Python/Node on 127.0.0.1)
                       → outbound HTTPS to OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Cohere
```

- **Firewall:** only 22, 80, 443 (Tier 1).
- **HTTPS + 301** from HTTP (Tier 1).
- **Nginx proxy** so the AI isn’t called on a weird public port (Tier 2).

Implement the backend in whichever you’re fastest in: **PHP** (often pairs with cheap shared hosting / WordPress), **Python Flask/FastAPI**, or **Node/Express**.

---

## 3. Making the bot “about you” (custom system prompt)

In your **server-only** script, build a prompt like:

```text
You are a concise assistant that answers ONLY using the facts below.
If something isn’t listed, say you don’t have that info and suggest emailing [your email] or viewing the Projects section.
Do not invent employers, dates, certifications, or skills.

=== PROFILE ===
[Name], [one-line headline]

Education:
- ...

Skills:
- ...

Projects (name + 1 sentence each):
- ...

Experience:
- ...

Contact:
Email: ..., LinkedIn: ...
```

Tune length: enough detail to answer FAQs, not a wall of text. **You iterate this** until answers feel accurate—that’s “custom system prompt.”

Optional: attach the **exact user question** as the user message; keep system prompt stable.

---

## 4. Improving “not good” portfolio without restarting

Prioritize **few, clear wins**:

1. **One strong hero line** — who you are + what role you’re aiming for (1 sentence).
2. **Projects** — each: problem, what you did, tech stack, link (GitHub/demo).
3. **Consistent typography and spacing** — one font pairing, readable line length, aligned sections.
4. **Mobile-friendly** — large tap targets on the AI form.
5. **Contact** — obvious email/LinkedIn; chatbot echoes “for official inquires use …”.

You don’t need a fancy framework if your stack is static + one backend route.

---

## 5. Checklist mapped to points

| Tier | You need |
|------|-----------|
| **1** | Live URL, custom domain DNS, Let’s Encrypt, HTTP→HTTPS 301, UFW-style firewall, proper vhost/server block |
| **2** | Server-side POST handler, nginx proxy for API route, contextual prompt about you, graceful errors on API failure |
| **3** | Short doc: OS, nginx/apache, PHP/Python/Node version, AI provider; paragraph on what the feature does and why; screenshot live; LinkedIn post with hashtags + link |

---

## 6. Timeline (aligned with slides)

By **end of week**: server + domain + SSL + test script hitting the API.

By **April 22**: nginx proxy wired, prompt working, ugly errors replaced with friendly messages.

Before **submission deadline**: screenshot, written explanation, LinkedIn post.

---

## 7. If you want hands-on code next

Paste or point to:

- Whether you host **plain HTML**, **WordPress**, or something else  
- Preferred backend (**PHP / Python / Node**)  
- Chosen provider (**OpenAI / Claude / Gemini / Cohere**)

Then we can sketch the exact nginx `location` block and a minimal `/api/chat` handler (still keeping your keys only on the server). If your portfolio files live in this workspace, share the folder path or open them and I can tie the frontend form into your layout.
